This chunk loads CVXR for convex constrained optimization, plotting and
diagnostic packages, and `here` for project-relative paths. The selected ridge
models are estimated with explicit quadratic objectives rather than a black
box fitting function so annual GDP constraints can be imposed directly.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load Libraries
library(CVXR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
```

The hidden setup chunk resolves the repository root and creates the ridge
model's figure, data-output, and serialized-model directories. These paths
keep generated artifacts together and do not change the statistical inputs.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Directory setup
project_dir <- here()
source_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "code", "R")

# Figure output path
figure_output_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "figures", "ridge_model")
dir.create(figure_output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Data output path
data_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "data")
data_output_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "predicted_data", "ridge_model")
dir.create(data_output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Model output path
model_output_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "code", "R", "model", "ridge_model")
dir.create(model_output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

This chunk loads shared plotting and comparison helpers. The latter supplies
the common 2020–2024/2025 OLS reference and diagnostic output functions used
to compare ridge with the other model families.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load source code
source(file.path(source_dir, "graph_utils.R"))
source(file.path(source_dir, "model_comparison_setup.R"))
```

### Load dataset

For this model, we will use the following training and testing datasets:

* `prediction_dataset.csv`: For prediction purposes

* `regression_dataset.csv`: For training and regression purposes

* `vnm_.csv`: For constraints purposes

All data sets have been cleaned and contain no missing values.

This chunk reads the regression panel, level-2 prediction features, national
GDP targets, and provincial 2025 GRDP-per-capita and population totals.
Official population values are converted from thousands to persons once so
their units agree with the level-2 population data used for calibration.

```{r}
# Regression Dataset
regression_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "training_data/regression_dataset.csv"))

# Prediction Dataset
prediction_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "training_data/prediction_dataset.csv"))

# National GDP totals used to constrain the regression fit
constrained_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "_vnm_indicators/vnm_level0_gdp.csv"))

# Provincial GRDP per-capita targets used to calibrate 2025 level-2 predictions
provincial_grdp_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir,
  "_vnm_indicators/vnm_GRDPpc.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Provincial population totals (thousands) used as the aggregation constraint
provincial_population_data <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir,
  "_vnm_indicators/vnm_population.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Provincial population data are in thousands; convert to persons.
provincial_population_data[, as.character(2020:2025)] <-
  provincial_population_data[, as.character(2020:2025)] * 1000
```


### Shared training and holdout setup

The shared setup converts regression population to persons, splits 2020–2024
from the 2025 holdout, standardizes the common features and outcome using
training-only statistics, and computes linear temporal extrapolation weights.
Its native OLS holdout reference is saved alongside the ridge outputs.
The chunk also extracts the scaled feature matrices for the ridge design.

```{r}
model_setup <- prepare_model_comparison_setup(regression_data)
regression_data <- model_setup$regression_data
training_data <- model_setup$training_data
holdout_data <- model_setup$holdout_data
training_years <- model_setup$training_years
holdout_year <- model_setup$holdout_year
feature_columns <- model_setup$feature_columns
feature_means <- model_setup$feature_means
feature_sds <- model_setup$feature_sds
temporal_extrapolation_weights <-
  model_setup$temporal_extrapolation_weights
ols_comparison <- fit_ols_comparison(model_setup)
ols_reference_predictions <- ols_comparison$holdout
ols_reference_predictions$residual <-
  ols_reference_predictions$actual - ols_reference_predictions$predicted
ols_reference_predictions$residual_scaled <-
  ols_reference_predictions$actual_scaled -
  ols_reference_predictions$predicted_scaled
write.csv(
  ols_reference_predictions,
  file.path(data_output_dir, "ols_reference_holdout_predictions.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

scaled_training <- as.matrix(training_data[paste0(feature_columns, "_scaled")])
scaled_holdout <- as.matrix(holdout_data[paste0(feature_columns, "_scaled")])
```


### Preliminaries
Supposed:

* \(y \in \mathbb{R}^n\): observed outcome vector. That is, `grdp_per_capita`.
* \(x_i \in \mathbb{R}^3\): standardized explanatory variables for observation \(i\): `mean_radiance`, `population`, and `pixel_count`.
* \(\alpha_t \in \mathbb{R}\): year-specific intercept for year \(t\).
* \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^3\): shared slopes for the explanatory variables.
* \(a_t \in \mathbb{R}\): specified national GDP total for year \(t\).
* \(\lambda\): ridge penalty.

The model uses data from 2020–2024 to train several ridge regression models with different values of \(\lambda\). The 2025 provincial data is kept separate and used to choose the best \(\lambda\) based on prediction RMSE.

The 2025 national GDP constraint is not used during this process, so the model must predict the 2025 provincial values without knowing the national GDP total.

Temporal extrapolation weights: Because 2025 is outside the training period, its year-specific intercept cannot be estimated directly from the training observations.

Instead, we compute temporal extrapolation weights based on a linear trend across the five training years. These weights extrapolate the year-specific intercepts to 2025.

The weights are calculated as:

\[ w_t = \frac{1}{T} + \frac{(t^*-\bar{t})(t-\bar{t})} {\sum_{j=1}^{T}(j-\bar{t})^2} \]

where:

- \(T\) is the number of training years.
- \(t\) represents an individual training year.
- \(t^*\) is the holdout year (2025).
- \(\bar{t}\) is the mean training year.

The resulting weights are used to construct the year-effect component of `X_holdout`. The standardized explanatory variables are appended to complete the holdout design matrix.

Each candidate model has a separate intercept for each training year but uses the same coefficients for all explanatory variables. The intercepts are not penalized, while the coefficients are penalized using ridge regression. All explanatory variables are standardized before fitting the models.

National GDP constraints are applied only to the training years (2020–2024). Candidate models are then evaluated against the actual 2025 provincial GRDP values using RMSE and \(R^2\).

After selecting the best \(\lambda\), the model is refitted using all available years (2020–2025) and used to generate Level-2 predictions.

This chunk builds the ridge design with one column per training-year
intercept and the three training-standardized features. For 2025, year-effect
columns use the shared linear-trend extrapolation weights instead of a
holdout-derived coefficient. It checks both matrices against the common setup,
then aligns population and annual national-GDP targets for the training
constraints.

```{r}
# Construct the training design matrix with year-specific intercepts.
training_data$year_factor <- factor(training_data$year, levels = training_years)
X_train <- cbind(
  model.matrix(~ 0 + year_factor, data = training_data),
  as.matrix(scaled_training)
)

# Reuse the shared setup's training-only temporal extrapolation weights.
time_extrapolation_weights <- temporal_extrapolation_weights

# Construct the holdout design matrix using extrapolated year effects.
X_holdout <- cbind(
  matrix(
    rep(time_extrapolation_weights, each = nrow(holdout_data)),
    nrow = nrow(holdout_data)
  ),
  as.matrix(scaled_holdout)
)
if (!isTRUE(all.equal(
      unname(X_train),
      unname(model_setup$X_train),
      check.attributes = FALSE
    )) ||
    !isTRUE(all.equal(
      unname(X_holdout),
      unname(model_setup$X_test),
      check.attributes = FALSE
    ))) {
  stop("Ridge model design matrices do not match the shared comparison setup.")
}


# Prepare population weights and annual GDP constraint targets.
training_population <- training_data$population
training_year <- training_data$year
target_gdp_training <- constrained_data$gdp[
  match(training_years, constrained_data$year)
]
y_train <- model_setup$y_train
y_holdout <- model_setup$y_test
y_train_raw <- model_setup$y_train_raw
y_holdout_raw <- model_setup$y_test_raw
```

### Optimization problem

For each candidate \(\lambda\), fit the shared standardized response on `X_train` and `y_train`. Predictions are returned to GRDP-per-capita units for the training-year national GDP constraints and 2025 holdout scoring:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\alpha,\beta}\quad &
\|y-\hat y\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
&\sum_{i:\,\mathrm{year}_i=t} P_i\hat y_i=a_t,
\quad t\in\{2020,\ldots,2024\},\\
&\hat y_{it}=\alpha_t+x_i^\top\beta,
\quad t\in\{2020,\ldots,2024\},\\
\quad \lambda\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
}
\]
Only the standardized feature slopes \(\beta\) are penalized. The yearly intercepts remain unpenalized. The 2025 intercept is predicted by linearly extrapolating the fitted 2020–2024 intercepts. This extrapolation uses training years only.


The following search evaluates 61 logarithmically spaced penalties from
\(10^{-3}\) through \(10^3\). For each \(\lambda\), CVXR minimizes
\(\|y-X\theta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2\), subject to the 2020–2024
population-weighted GDP equalities. Only feature slopes are penalized;
year-specific intercepts are not. Each fitted candidate predicts the 2025
holdout, where minimum RMSE selects \(\lambda\); holdout outcomes are used
only for selection and evaluation, never in fitting the candidate.

```{r}
# Define a logarithmically spaced ridge penalty grid from 10^-3 to 10^3.
lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = 61)

# Determine the total number of model parameters and identify the indices corresponding to explanatory-variable coefficients.
training_parameter_count <- ncol(X_train)
feature_parameter_indices <- (length(training_years) + 1):training_parameter_count

# Initialize storage for the estimated coefficients, holdout predictions, and solver statuses across all candidate lambda values.
holdout_coefficients <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = training_parameter_count,
  ncol = length(lambda_grid)
)

holdout_predictions <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = length(y_holdout),
  ncol = length(lambda_grid)
)

holdout_status <- character(length(lambda_grid))


# Evaluate each candidate lambda using constrained ridge regression.
for (lambda_index in seq_along(lambda_grid)) {

  # Define the optimization variable representing regression coefficients.
  ridge_beta <- Variable(training_parameter_count)

  # Calculate fitted values for the training observations.
  ridge_fitted <- X_train %*% ridge_beta

  # Construct annual national GDP constraints.
  training_constraints <- lapply(seq_along(training_years), function(i) {
    idx <- which(training_year == training_years[i])

    sum_entries(
      training_population[idx] *
        (model_setup$response_mean +
          model_setup$response_sd * ridge_fitted[idx])
    ) /
      target_gdp_training[i] == 1
  })

  # Define the constrained ridge regression optimization problem.
  ridge_problem <- Problem(
    Minimize(
      sum_squares(y_train - ridge_fitted) +
        lambda_grid[lambda_index] *
        sum_squares(ridge_beta[feature_parameter_indices])
    ),
    training_constraints
  )

  # Solve the optimization problem
  suppressMessages({
  ridge_result <- solve(
    ridge_problem,
    solver = "CLARABEL",
    max_iter = 1000
  )})

  # Record the solver status for the current lambda.
  holdout_status[lambda_index] <- ridge_result$status

  # Stop execution if the optimization problem does not return
  # an acceptable solution.
  if (!ridge_result$status %in% c("optimal", "optimal_inaccurate")) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Training ridge fit failed for lambda=%g with solver status: %s",
      lambda_grid[lambda_index],
      ridge_result$status
    ))
  }

  # Store the estimated regression coefficients.
  holdout_coefficients[, lambda_index] <-
    as.numeric(value(ridge_beta))

  # Generate predictions for the 2025 holdout observations using the estimated coefficients and the holdout design matrix.
  holdout_predictions[, lambda_index] <-
    as.vector(X_holdout %*% holdout_coefficients[, lambda_index]) *
      model_setup$response_sd + model_setup$response_mean
}


# Calculate the total sum of squares of the observed 2025 GRDP per capita values for the holdout R-squared calculation.
holdout_total_sum_squares <- sum(
  (y_holdout_raw - mean(y_holdout_raw))^2
)

# Evaluate predictive performance for each candidate lambda.
lambda_results <- data.frame(
  lambda = lambda_grid,

  # Calculate the root mean squared prediction error.
  holdout_RMSE = apply(holdout_predictions, 2, function(fit) {
    sqrt(mean((y_holdout_raw - fit)^2))
  }),

  # Calculate the holdout coefficient of determination.
  holdout_R_squared = apply(holdout_predictions, 2, function(fit) {
    1 - sum((y_holdout_raw - fit)^2) / holdout_total_sum_squares
  }),

  # Retain the optimization status for each candidate lambda.
  solver_status = holdout_status
)


# Export the lambda evaluation results for subsequent analysis.
write.csv(
  lambda_results,
  file.path(data_output_dir, "ridge_lambda_grid_metrics.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Select the regularization parameter that minimizes the 2025 holdout RMSE.
selected_index <- which.min(lambda_results$holdout_RMSE)
selected_lambda <- lambda_results$lambda[selected_index]

# Extract the holdout predictions corresponding to the selected lambda.
best_holdout_predictions <- holdout_predictions[, selected_index]

# Calculate prediction residuals for the selected model.
holdout_residuals <- y_holdout_raw - best_holdout_predictions

# Report the selected regularization parameter and evaluation metrics.
cat(sprintf(
  "Selected lambda by minimum 2025 holdout RMSE: %.8g\n",
  selected_lambda
))
```

This chunk visualizes holdout RMSE and \(R^2\) across the log-spaced penalty
grid. The vertical line and highlighted point mark the RMSE-selected
\(\lambda\); plotting both metrics shows the accuracy tradeoff without
changing the selection rule.

```{r}
# Define the output path for the lambda evaluation figure.
lambda_plot_path <- file.path(
  figure_output_dir,
  "ridge_lambda_grid_metrics.png"
)

# Open a PNG graphics device for saving the diagnostic plots.
grDevices::png(
  lambda_plot_path,
  width = 2000,
  height = 900,
  res = 160
)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))


# p1: 2025 holdout RMSE across candidate lambda values.
plot(
  lambda_results$lambda,
  lambda_results$holdout_RMSE,
  type = "l",
  col = "#0072B2",
  xlab = expression(lambda),
  ylab = "2025 holdout RMSE",
  main = "Ridge penalty grid: 2025 RMSE",
  log = "x",
  yaxt = "n"
)

# Highlight the selected lambda and distinguish it from other candidates.
points(
  lambda_results$lambda,
  lambda_results$holdout_RMSE,
  pch = 19,
  col = ifelse(
    seq_len(nrow(lambda_results)) == selected_index,
    "#D55E00",
    "#0072B2"
  )
)

# Generate readable y-axis tick marks for the RMSE values.
rmse_ticks <- pretty(lambda_results$holdout_RMSE)

axis(
  2,
  at = rmse_ticks,
  labels = formatC(rmse_ticks, format = "f", digits = 8)
)

# Add a vertical reference line indicating the selected lambda.
abline(
  v = selected_lambda,
  lty = 2,
  col = "#D55E00"
)


# p2: 2025 holdout R-squared across candidate lambda values.
plot(
  lambda_results$lambda,
  lambda_results$holdout_R_squared,
  type = "l",
  col = "#0072B2",
  xlab = expression(lambda),
  ylab = expression("2025 holdout " * R^2),
  main = "Ridge penalty grid: 2025 R-squared",
  log = "x",
  yaxt = "n"
)

# Highlight the selected lambda and distinguish it from other candidates.
points(
  lambda_results$lambda,
  lambda_results$holdout_R_squared,
  pch = 19,
  col = ifelse(
    seq_len(nrow(lambda_results)) == selected_index,
    "#D55E00",
    "#0072B2"
  )
)

# Generate readable y-axis tick marks for the R-squared values.
r_squared_ticks <- pretty(lambda_results$holdout_R_squared)

axis(
  2,
  at = r_squared_ticks,
  labels = formatC(r_squared_ticks, format = "f", digits = 8)
)

# Add a vertical reference line indicating the selected lambda.
abline(
  v = selected_lambda,
  lty = 2,

)


# Close the graphics device and finalize the PNG output.
invisible(grDevices::dev.off())

# Include the saved figure in the rendered R Markdown document.
knitr::include_graphics(
  normalizePath(lambda_plot_path),
  rel_path = FALSE
)
```

### Refit selected model on all years

After selecting \(\lambda\) using only 2025 holdout RMSE, refit the constrained ridge model on all available years.
This final fit is used only to generate the 2025 level-2 predictions.
The reported holdout metrics above remain predictions from models trained on 2020–2024.

The final model refit uses the selected \(\lambda\) on all available years
(2020–2025) so it can estimate a direct 2025 year effect for level-2
prediction. It reapplies the same feature scaling, penalizes only feature
slopes, and imposes one population-weighted national GDP equality for each
year in the refit. This refit does not replace the earlier holdout scores.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# All years
years <- sort(unique(regression_data$year))

# Convert year into a factor with explicitly ordered levels.
regression_data$year_factor <- factor(
  regression_data$year,
  levels = years
)

# Standardize all predictor variables using the feature means and standard deviations calculated previously.
scaled_all <- scale(
  regression_data[feature_columns],
  center = feature_means,
  scale = feature_sds
)

# Construct the full design matrix:
# - Year-specific intercept columns (one for each year).
# - Standardized predictor columns.
X <- cbind(
  model.matrix(~ 0 + year_factor, data = regression_data),
  as.matrix(scaled_all)
)

# Extract the response variable, calendar year, and population.
y <- regression_data$grdp_per_capita
year <- regression_data$year
population <- regression_data$population

# Record the total number of model parameters.
p <- ncol(X)

# Identify the parameter indices corresponding to the predictors.
feature_parameter_indices <- (length(years) + 1):p

# Retrieve the national GDP target corresponding to each year.
target_gdp <- constrained_data$gdp[
  match(years, constrained_data$year)
]

# Define the optimization variable containing all model coefficients.
final_beta <- Variable(p)

# Calculate fitted GRDP per capita for every observation.
final_fitted <- X %*% final_beta

# Construct one national GDP constraint for each year.
final_constraints <- lapply(seq_along(years), function(i) {
  idx <- which(year == years[i])

  sum_entries(
    population[idx] * final_fitted[idx]
  ) / target_gdp[i] == 1
})

# Define the final constrained ridge regression problem.
final_problem <- Problem(
  Minimize(
    sum_squares(y - final_fitted) +
      selected_lambda * sum_squares(
        final_beta[feature_parameter_indices]
      )
  ),
  final_constraints
)

# Solve
final_result <- solve(
  final_problem,
  solver = "CLARABEL",
  max_iter = 1000
)
if (!final_result$status %in% c("optimal", "optimal_inaccurate")) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "Final all-years ridge refit failed with solver status: %s",
    final_result$status
  ))
}

# Extract the estimated regression coefficients as a numeric vector.
beta_hat <- as.numeric(value(final_beta))

# Calculate the final fitted GRDP per capita values using the estimated coefficients.
predictions <- as.vector(X %*% beta_hat)

# Construct a diagnostic table to evaluate the annual GDP constraints.
final_constraint_check <- data.frame(
  year = years,
  predicted_total = vapply(years, function(t) {
    idx <- which(year == t)
    sum(population[idx] * predictions[idx])
  }, numeric(1)),
  target_total = target_gdp
)

# Calculate the difference between the predicted and target totals.
final_constraint_check$difference <-
  final_constraint_check$predicted_total -
  final_constraint_check$target_total

# Verify that all annual GDP constraints are satisfied
if (any(
  abs(final_constraint_check$difference) >
    1e-8 * pmax(abs(final_constraint_check$target_total), 1)
)) {
  stop("Final ridge refit does not satisfy the annual GDP constraints.")
}

# Display the constraint-checking results for all years.
print(final_constraint_check, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Statistical Summary

Lambda selection uses 2025 holdout predictions from models fitted on
2020–2024. The split comparison tables and diagnostics report training and
holdout performance against the shared OLS reference fit on `X_train`,
`y_train`.

This chunk compiles split-specific ridge and OLS residuals, writes common
training/holdout diagnostics and comparison metrics, and reports \(R^2\) and
RMSE for both methods. It converts the selected standardized ridge fit back
to original outcome units before comparing the two models.

```{r}
# Calculate OLS holdout residuals as the difference between
# observed and predicted GRDP per capita values.
ols_holdout_predictions <- ols_reference_predictions$predicted
ols_holdout_residuals <- y_holdout_raw - ols_holdout_predictions

# Retrieve the previously calculated constrained ridge
# holdout residuals.
ridge_residuals <- holdout_residuals

# Extract the ridge coefficients corresponding to the
# selected regularization parameter (lambda).
selected_ridge_coefficients <- holdout_coefficients[, selected_index]

# Generate fitted values for the training observations using
# the selected ridge coefficients.
# Transform predictions back to the original GRDP-per-capita
# scale using the response standard deviation and mean.
ridge_training_predictions <- as.vector(
  X_train %*% selected_ridge_coefficients
) * model_setup$response_sd + model_setup$response_mean

# Generate model comparison diagnostics for the constrained
# ridge model and the OLS reference model.
# Evaluate both models on the training and holdout datasets.
# Save diagnostic data and figures to their respective directories.
comparison_metrics <- write_model_comparison_diagnostics(
  model_name = "Constrained ridge",
  training_data = training_data,
  holdout_data = holdout_data,
  training_fitted = ridge_training_predictions,
  holdout_fitted = best_holdout_predictions,
  ols_training = ols_comparison$training$predicted,
  ols_holdout = ols_comparison$holdout$predicted,
  data_output_dir = data_output_dir,
  figure_output_dir = figure_output_dir,
  file_prefix = "ridge_model",
  feature_columns = feature_columns
)

# Extract R-squared and RMSE for the holdout observations.
holdout_model_stats <- comparison_metrics[
  comparison_metrics$split == "holdout",
  c("model", "R_squared", "RMSE")
]

# Extract R-squared and RMSE for the training observations.
training_model_stats <- comparison_metrics[
  comparison_metrics$split == "training",
  c("model", "R_squared", "RMSE")
]

# Display holdout performance metrics for both models.
print(holdout_model_stats, row.names = FALSE)

# Report the selected regularization parameter and the
# corresponding 2025 holdout RMSE and R-squared.
cat(sprintf(
  "Selected lambda: %.8g; 2025 holdout RMSE: %.6f; holdout R-squared: %.6f\n",
  selected_lambda,
  holdout_model_stats$RMSE[1],
  holdout_model_stats$R_squared[1]
))

# Extract holdout RMSE values for the constrained ridge
# and OLS reference models, respectively.
ridge_rmse <- holdout_model_stats$RMSE[1]
ols_rmse <- holdout_model_stats$RMSE[2]

# Calculate and report the absolute and percentage differences
# between the ridge and OLS holdout RMSE values.
# Determine whether the ridge model has higher or lower RMSE
# than the OLS reference model.
cat(sprintf(
  "2025 holdout ridge RMSE (lambda=%.8g) is %.6f GRDP-per-capita units (%.2f%%) %s than OLS reference RMSE.\n",
  selected_lambda,
  abs(ridge_rmse - ols_rmse),
  abs(ridge_rmse - ols_rmse) / ols_rmse * 100,
  if (ridge_rmse >= ols_rmse) "higher" else "lower"
))
```

### 2025 holdout fit and residual diagnostics

The first figure compares 2025 holdout observations with predictions from the
selected constrained ridge model and an unconstrained OLS reference. Residual
panels show holdout errors against predictions and predictors. With only one
holdout year, year-to-year diagnostics are not applicable; these plots are
descriptive checks rather than formal inference.

The first diagnostics chunk writes a province-level actual/prediction table
and plots ridge and OLS holdout fits against the 45-degree reference. It
orders the printed table by absolute ridge residual so the largest holdout
errors are easy to inspect.

```{r holdout-diagnostics, echo=FALSE}
training_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  province = holdout_data$province,
  actual = y_holdout_raw,
  constrained_fitted = best_holdout_predictions,
  constrained_residual = ridge_residuals,
  ols_fitted = ols_holdout_predictions,
  ols_residual = ols_holdout_residuals,
  year = factor(holdout_data$year),
  mean_radiance = holdout_data$mean_radiance,
  population = holdout_data$population,
  pixel_count = holdout_data$pixel_count
)
holdout_predictions_table <- data.frame(
  province = training_diagnostics$province,
  year = holdout_year,
  actual = training_diagnostics$actual,
  ridge_prediction = training_diagnostics$constrained_fitted,
  ridge_residual = training_diagnostics$constrained_residual,
  ols_prediction = training_diagnostics$ols_fitted,
  ols_residual = training_diagnostics$ols_residual
)
holdout_predictions_path <- file.path(
  data_output_dir,
  "ridge_model_2025_holdout_predictions.csv"
)
write.csv(

)
print(

    order(abs(holdout_predictions_table$ridge_residual), decreasing = TRUE),
  ],
  row.names = FALSE
)

actual_fitted_path <- file.path(

grDevices::png(actual_fitted_path, width = 1800, height = 1100, res = 160)
```

### 2025 Level-2 Predictions

The model first predicts GRDP per capita for each level-2 unit using the 2025 intercept and the same means and standard deviations used to standardize the training data.
Next, we adjust these predictions so that their population weighted total matches the province's reported 2025 GRDP per capita multiplied by its total population.
To do this, we add the same adjustment \(\delta_j\) to every level-2 prediction within province \(j\):

\[ \tilde y_{ij} = \hat y_{ij} + \delta_j \]

The adjustment is calculated as:

\[ \delta_j = \frac{g_jN_j-\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}\hat y_{ij}} {\sum_{i\in j}P_{ij}} \]

where \(g_j\) is the province's reported GRDP per capita, \(N_j\) is its total population, and \(P_{ij}\) is the population of level-2 unit \(i\).

The code uses the all-years design and training-derived feature scales, checks
the aggregation equality for every province, then writes prediction and
constraint-check tables and the final model RDS. Official provincial
populations have already been converted to persons; level-2 population values
are already persons and must not be multiplied by 1,000 again.

```{r}
prediction_features <- as.matrix(prediction_data[feature_columns])
grdp_pc_2025 <- provincial_grdp_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_grdp_data$province)
]
province_population_2025 <- provincial_population_data[["2025"]][
  match(prediction_data$level_1, provincial_population_data$province)
]
if (anyNA(province_population_2025) ||
    any(!is.finite(province_population_2025)) ||
    any(province_population_2025 <= 0)) {
  stop("Missing or invalid 2025 population total for a prediction province.")
}

prediction_data$year_factor <- factor(prediction_data$year, levels = years)
scaled_prediction <- scale(
  prediction_data[feature_columns],
  center = feature_means,
  scale = feature_sds
)
prediction_X <- cbind(
  model.matrix(~ 0 + year_factor, data = prediction_data),
  as.matrix(scaled_prediction)
)

raw_level2_predictions <- as.vector(prediction_X %*% beta_hat)
province_names <- sort(unique(prediction_data$level_1))
province_adjustments <- setNames(numeric(length(province_names)), province_names)

for (province in province_names) {
  idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)
  level2_population <- sum(prediction_data$population[idx])
  if (!is.finite(level2_population) || level2_population <= 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Province %s has no positive level-2 population.", province))
  }

  province_index <- match(province, prediction_data$level_1)
  target_total <- grdp_pc_2025[province_index] *
    province_population_2025[province_index]
  raw_total <- sum(
    prediction_data$population[idx] * raw_level2_predictions[idx]
  )
  province_adjustments[[province]] <- (target_total - raw_total) /
    level2_population
}

prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita <- raw_level2_predictions
prediction_data$province_adjustment <-
  province_adjustments[prediction_data$level_1]
prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita <-
  prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita + prediction_data$province_adjustment
prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025 <- grdp_pc_2025

province_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(province_names, function(province) {
  idx <- which(prediction_data$level_1 == province)
  province_index <- match(province, prediction_data$level_1)
  province_population <- province_population_2025[province_index]
  target_total <- prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025[idx[1]] *
    province_population
  predicted_total <- sum(
    prediction_data$population[idx] *
      prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita[idx]
  )

  data.frame(
    province = province,
    population = province_population,
    level2_population = sum(prediction_data$population[idx]),
    target_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025[idx[1]],
    target_total_grdp = target_total,
    predicted_total_grdp = predicted_total,
    difference = predicted_total - target_total
  )
}))

if (any(abs(province_check$difference) >
        1e-8 * pmax(abs(province_check$target_total_grdp), 1))) {
  stop("Calibrated level-2 predictions do not match all provincial GDP targets.")
}
write.csv(
  province_check,
  file.path(data_output_dir, "ridge_model_province_constraint_check.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

level2_predictions <- data.frame(
  level_2 = prediction_data$name,
  level_1 = prediction_data$level_1,
  year = prediction_data$year,
  population = prediction_data$population,
  province_population_2025 = province_population_2025,
  ridge_lambda = rep(selected_lambda, nrow(prediction_data)),
  raw_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$raw_grdp_per_capita,
  province_adjustment = prediction_data$province_adjustment,
  predicted_grdp_per_capita = prediction_data$predicted_grdp_per_capita,
  province_grdp_per_capita_target_2025 =
    prediction_data$grdp_per_capita_target_2025
)
prediction_output <- file.path(
  data_output_dir,
  "ridge_model_level2_predictions.csv"
)
write.csv(level2_predictions, prediction_output, row.names = FALSE)

ridge_model <- list(
  coefficients = beta_hat,
  variable_names = colnames(X),
  years = years,
  feature_columns = feature_columns,
  feature_means = feature_means,
  feature_sds = feature_sds,
  selected_lambda = selected_lambda,
  solver = "CLARABEL",
  solver_status = final_result$status,
  objective_value = final_result$value,
  holdout_metrics = holdout_model_stats,
  holdout_lambda_grid = lambda_results
)
model_output <- file.path(model_output_dir, "constrained_ridge_model.rds")
saveRDS(ridge_model, model_output)

print(province_check, row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved ridge model to", model_output, "\n")
cat("Wrote level-2 predictions to", prediction_output, "\n")
head(level2_predictions)
```
